import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source tables
source_files = {
    "Source6_10_0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_0.csv",
    "Source6_10_1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_1.csv",
    "Source6_10_2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_2.csv",
    "Source6_10_3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_3.csv",
    "Source6_10_4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_4.csv",
    "Source6_10_5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_5.csv",
    "Source6_10_6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/training_6.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_0"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '0.0075805085']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_1"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '0.016157143']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_2"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '6.9']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_3"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '20.3333']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_4"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '301.0']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_5"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '0.0179']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["Source6_10_6"], index_col=0)  # ['2012-12-05', '0.17657143']

# Step 2: All source tables share the key column '2012-12-05'.
# We will join all tables on this key column to form the target table.
# The target schema columns are:
# ['2012-12-05': string, '301.0': integer, '0.0075805085': float, '0.0179': float, '6.9': float,
#  '0.17657143': float, '20.3333': float, '0.016157143': float]

# Step 3: Merge all dataframes on '2012-12-05' using inner join to keep only dates present in all sources.
# This ensures all columns are present for each date.

# Merge order chosen arbitrarily but consistent:
df_merge = df4.merge(df0, on='2012-12-05', how='inner') \
              .merge(df5, on='2012-12-05', how='inner') \
              .merge(df2, on='2012-12-05', how='inner') \
              .merge(df6, on='2012-12-05', how='inner') \
              .merge(df3, on='2012-12-05', how='inner') \
              .merge(df1, on='2012-12-05', how='inner')

# Step 4: Data type conversions to match target schema
# '2012-12-05' as string (date string)
df_merge['2012-12-05'] = df_merge['2012-12-05'].astype(str)

# '301.0' as integer
df_merge['301.0'] = pd.to_numeric(df_merge['301.0'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# The rest columns as float
float_cols = ['0.0075805085', '0.0179', '6.9', '0.17657143', '20.3333', '0.016157143']
for col in float_cols:
    df_merge[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_merge[col], errors='coerce')

# Step 5: Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['2012-12-05', '301.0', '0.0075805085', '0.0179', '6.9', '0.17657143', '20.3333', '0.016157143']
df_target = df_merge[target_columns]

# Step 6: Write the resulting dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_10/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
